name: MIT Solve
funding_text: $100K per Solver + prize layers
eligibility: Global incl. India

name: MLH Fellowship
funding_text: Need-based stipend (aggregators cite $1K–5K, unconfirmed)
eligibility: 18+, worldwide, remote; students/recent grads; 12 wks

name: Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund
funding_text: Up to $25,000 per project, equity-free; can go to individuals. Deadline: current round Sep 15 – Oct 15, 2026 (verified); next Jan 31, 2027.
eligibility: "Anyone directly involved in species conservation" — no age limit, no degree requirement, individuals or orgs; global without regional discrimination. India-open.
deadline_text: - Funding: Up to $25,000 per project, equity-free; can go to individuals. Deadline: current round Sep 15 – Oct 15, 2026 (verified); next Jan 31, 2027.
why_easy: Favors underfunded non-charismatic species, so conservation-tech founders rarely think of it; invisible in startup circles.

name: MSME Idea Hackathon
org: Ministry of MSME, Govt. of India
funding_text: Up to ₹15 lakh per idea (85% govt contribution) via approved Host Institutes (incl. IIT host institutes) for a working prototype.
eligibility: Any Indian citizen 18–60 — students (with valid ID), MSMEs, freelancers, researchers, independent innovators. No affiliation required. India-open.
deadline_text: Hackathon 6.0 closed Jul 21, 2026; 7.0 unverified; underlying scheme runs year-round via Host Institutes.
why_easy: Govt scheme with low visibility among students; most entries come from MSMEs, so a student applicant faces a thin pool.

name: Nagarathna Memorial Grant (NMG) 2026
org: Thejesh GN, co-supported by FOSS United Foundation
funding_text: No-strings grant; 2026 pool ₹5 lakh, individual awards historically ~₹1,00,000+.
eligibility: Anyone doing meaningful work in India. India-open. No age/stage bar stated.
why_easy: Word-of-mouth inside the IndiaFOSS community; trust-based, minimal bureaucracy; invisible outside it.

name: Narisetti Grants
funding_text: $100–$1,000 micro-grants.
eligibility: Global applications welcome, individual builders. India-open.
deadline_text: Rolling (apply via links on his X profile; if no form is visible, DM @NarisettiGrants).
why_easy: Run from a personal X account, not an institution — invisible outside builder Twitter; near-zero application friction.

name: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
funding_text: No cash — recognition + possible NASA Center Winners Celebration
eligibility: Worldwide, all ages; teams ≤6; in-person or virtual

name: National Geographic Society — RFPs
funding_text: Per-RFP amounts; e.g., "The Human Thread" storytelling RFP
eligibility: 18+, international incl. India

name: NIDHI Seed Support System (via approved TBIs)
funding_text: Average ₹25 lakh, up to ₹100 lakh per startup (grant/debt/equity-linked, TBI-dependent).
eligibility: Indian startups (≥51% Indian promoters), ≥3 months TBI residency (resident or virtual); preference DPIIT-registered. India-open.
deadline_text: Annual call cycle starting January; TBI-specific calls vary; next unverified.
why_easy: You apply to a specific TBI, not a national pool — competition is per-incubator, and many TBIs outside metros get few quality applications.

name: NIDHI-EIR
funding_text: ₹10–30K/mo (max ₹3.6L) for 12–18 mo
eligibility: Indian citizens; degree + experience; preference under-35; full-time, no other income

name: NIDHI-PRAYAS
funding_text: Up to ₹10L idea→prototype + lab/mentorship/IP support
eligibility: Individual innovators 18+ (citizens) or early startups

name: NLnet Foundation
funding_text: €5,000–€50,000 initial (up to €500K lifetime cap). Non-dilutive, milestone-based; everything open-licensed.
eligibility: Individuals and informal orgs welcome — no legal entity or university needed; young people explicitly welcome. ⚠️
why_easy: <1-hour application; highly technical niche; most student founders never consider EU open-internet funding.

name: NSRCEL (IIM Bangalore)
funding_text: Top-performing startups (typically top 3 of ~30/cohort) get ₹5 lakh non-dilutive grants (milestone-linked), zero equity, zero fees. (Sibling: Women Startup Programme — ₹10L grants for women-founded ventures.)
eligibility: Pan-India founders, all sectors — NOT restricted to IIMB students/alumni. India-open.
why_easy: B-school incubator in the shadow of famous govt schemes; small cohorts; women's track has national reach with niche awareness.

name: One Young World Leading Scholarship
funding_text: Summit delegate access, catering, programming; travel case-by-case
eligibility: 18–35, demonstrated positive-change record; India eligible

name: Open Technology Fund
funding_text: $10,000–$900,000 (most $50K–$200K); performance-based contracts. Smallest tier fits a focused student project.
eligibility: Individuals or orgs (for-profit or nonprofit), all ages, no nationality restriction (India-open; only OFAC-sanctioned excluded). Preference for first-time applicants and Global South practitioners.
deadline_text: Rolling — concept note first, decision ~6–8 weeks.
why_easy: Niche internet-freedom framing; few student builders apply; explicit preference for Global South newcomers.

name: OpenAI Safety Fellowship
funding_text: Paid residency
eligibility: Monthly stipend + compute + mentorship

name: OSV Fellowship
funding_text: Up to $100K (+ grants of ≥$10K through the same form).
eligibility: Anywhere in the world, any age (India-open).
why_easy: New-ish program; calendar it for January.

name: Parallel18
org: Puerto Rico Science, Technology & Research Trust
funding_text: ⚠️ Historic $40K equity-free grant REPLACED in 2026 by a $100,000 investment (terms unverified) — verify current terms before applying. P18 Ventures follow-on for alumni.
eligibility: Open to companies from any country (only Trust program open to foreigners); must incorporate in US/PR and live in PR for 16 weeks. India-open.
why_easy: Requires moving to Puerto Rico; ~700 applications/generation; near-zero Indian awareness outside LatAm.

name: Pear Fellows
funding_text: Network/career program (no cash)
eligibility: Enrolled undergrad/MBA/PhD; US-university focused

name: Prime Minister's Research Fellows (PMRF)
funding_text: ₹70K–80K/mo (yrs 1–5) + ₹2L/yr research grant
eligibility: India; direct/lateral entry at PMRF-granting institutes incl. IIT Bombay
deadline_text: Unverified — no reliable central deadline found

name: Quad Fellowship
funding_text: $20K stipend + cohort programming
eligibility: India explicitly eligible; entering STEM master's/PhD in the US

name: QuickFire Challenges
funding_text: $25K–100K grant per winner + JLABS residency + mentorship
eligibility: Entrepreneurs/academics/startups worldwide; rotating themes
deadline_text: Rolling themes; watch for new challenges

name: Resolution Project — Social Venture Challenge / Fellowship
funding_text: $3K–$5K seed + mentorship + pro bono
eligibility: Current undergrads; youth teams + adult "Ally"; via Challenges at partner conferences

name: Rhodes Scholarship (India)
funding_text: Fully funded Oxford postgraduate (fees, stipend, travel, visa/IHS)
eligibility: Indian citizenship, study/residency in India, recent grad; 5 India scholarships

name: Rice Business Plan Competition
funding_text: $1M+ in investment, cash, in-kind; 2025 awarded $2M; grand prize ~$350,000 (convertible note); all 42 competing teams guaranteed cash.
eligibility: Student teams from universities worldwide (India incl.) — but requires ≥2 current student founders incl. ONE graduate-degree-seeking student (an undergrad needs a master's/PhD co-founder). ≤$250K raised. No application fees.
deadline_text: 2027 cycle unverified (apps typically open fall, invites Feb).
why_easy: Only 42 teams selected globally; grad-student requirement filters most undergrad teams; Indian universities rarely apply. Pitching to 300+ angels/VCs over 3 days is itself the prize.

name: Roddenberry Catalyst Fund
org: The Roddenberry Foundation (family foundation, Star Trek legacy)
funding_text: Up to $15,000, equity-free, rolling. (Sibling: Roddenberry Fellowship — $50,000, 12-month leadership fellowship; India eligibility unverified.)
eligibility: Individuals 18+, teams, nonprofits, social enterprises, for-profits; global (non-sanctioned). India-open. Early-stage.
why_easy: Sci-fi association makes serious founders overlook it; small ticket + simple rolling application.

name: Rufford Foundation
funding_text: 1st grant up to £7,000 (equity-free), then £8K → £12K → £18K staged follow-ons.
eligibility: Early-career conservationists (priority MSc/PhD or ≤3 yrs post-grad — undergrads explicitly NOT eligible, flag for later); projects in eligible developing countries; India is on the eligible list → India-open.
why_easy: Obscure UK micro-foundation; strict niche criteria (fieldwork only, no pure research/conferences) self-filters applicants.

name: Samsung
funding_text: Top 4: incubation grants worth ₹2 crore (split) at IIT Delhi; top 20: ₹20 lakh; top 40: ₹8 lakh (+ devices, mentorship). Equity-free.
eligibility: Students 14–22, India only, teams of 3–5. India-open.
why_easy: India-student-only team format; serious founder-types overlook it as a "student competition."

name: SBI Youth for India Fellowship
funding_text: Stipend fellowship (not a seed grant)
eligibility: Indian graduates/young professionals; 13-mo rural placement

name: Schaeffler India
funding_text: ₹2 lakh grant each + mentorship, industry exposure, ecosystem access.
eligibility: 10 social innovators; entrepreneurs from Tier II/III and rural India prioritized. India-only → India-open.
deadline_text: Announced July 2026; application status unverified (likely open/imminent).
why_easy: A car-parts company giving social-innovation money is so obscure founders never associate it with grants; only 10 slots; rural tilt filters urban elite competition.

name: Schmidt AI in Science fellowships
funding_text: Independent fellowships (2-yr and 4-yr)
eligibility: Postdoc-level at partner institutions (e.g., Imperial, EPFL)

name: Schmidt Science Fellows

eligibility: PhD candidates at nominating partner institutions

name: Schwarzman Scholars

eligibility: Global; bachelor's before Aug 2027; 18–29 on Aug 1, 2027

name: Scientific Fellowships (Medical Sciences + Climate & Health)

eligibility: Master's/PhD/medical students worldwide; non-German students must host at a German institution

name: Seeding The Future Global Food System Challenge

eligibility: Orgs (nonprofit, academic, early for-profit) any country incl. India

name: She Loves Tech

name: Shell E4 Startup Hub (India)

why_easy: Sector-narrowed energy/climate deep-tech; positioned as a "platform, not an accelerator"; far fewer applicants than generalist accelerators.

name: Shuttleworth Foundation
org: Shuttleworth Foundation (Mark Shuttleworth / Ubuntu founder's family foundation)
funding_text: One year's salary equivalent + expenses/travel + project funding (historically up to $275,000/yr). Effectively equity-free.

name: SINE IIT Bombay

eligibility: IIT Bombay students/recent grads/alumni-founded startups — institute-restricted (~10K people), which is exactly the point. India-open (IITB-only).
deadline_text: Ongoing calls on SINE portal; next unverified.
why_easy: Restricted to the IITB pool — zero competition with the general startup population; obscure outside IITB.

name: Smart India Hackathon (SIH)
org: MoE Innovation Cell + AICTE, Govt. of India
funding_text: ₹1.5 lakh cash per winning team per problem statement (Software); runners-up ₹25,000. ~271 problem statements = ~271 winning slots.

deadline_text: SIH 2025 finale Dec 2025; SIH 2026 registrations typically open Sep–Oct — watch now.
why_easy: Per-problem-statement competition at nodal centres is manageable; even losing finalists get strong resume value from solving real government problems.

name: Social Alpha (Tata Trusts ecosystem)

deadline_text: Challenge-based, intermittent; no confirmed 2026 call found (org alive per Tata Trusts FY25 filings).

name: Social Impact Award India

deadline_text: 2026 cycle closed Aug 31, 2026; next annual cycle ~mid-2027 (unverified).
why_easy: Very young org (~20K community), little Indian awareness; free application + free pre-application support.

name: SPARK Grants 2026

eligibility: Youth-led, women-led, Indigenous/community orgs, all WHO regions incl. India; org ≥2 yrs

name: The/Nudge

name: Watson Institute Fellowships
funding_text: Up to $6,000 seed (Flagship) / $1,000 (Western Union track); fully-funded participation.

eligibility: Women entrepreneurs in India
